name: Public telegraph service in colonial India
summary: From 1855 telegraph offices in British colonial India offered message service to the public, letting ordinary people send fast long-distance messages.
description: Telegraph offices offering message service to the public in British colonial India.
tier_reason: A specific community-facing use or availability in electrical communication, power or computing.
why: The East India Company government wanted fast communication to administer and defend a large territory, and adapted electric telegraphy already in use in Britain and elsewhere.

date.basis: Evidence for this dated community entry; not necessarily the first possible use.

events.caveats: Abstract only; individual class, regional and price barriers remain unassessed. The book abstract does not specify tariffs, languages, eligibility or how broadly access extended.

contributions.resource: Sought to send messages when the service opened to public use.
